messages:
anya: heads-up, starting onboarding for robinia-embed-v1. ran quick shorttail bench, fp16 looks good but int8 shows recall drop + tiny dense clusters in UMAP. need a quick sync.

ben: which dataset and numbers?

anya: dataset=shorttail-collection-3 (prod short queries + synth paraphrases). quick metrics: albatross-v2 fp16 r@1=0.78 r@5=0.92 silhouette=0.42; robinia-v1 fp16 r@1=0.81 r@5=0.94 silhouette=0.45; robinia-v1 int8 (per-channel symmetric) r@1=0.66 r@5=0.85 silhouette=0.28.

carlos: large delta. quant config? calib set?

anya: used CalSet100k. command: `python quantize.py --model robinia-v1 --mode int8 --calib CalSet100k --per_channel`. tried per-tensor asymmetric -> r@1 ~0.69, silhouette ~0.30.

ben: did you check embedding norms and cosine distributions?

anya: yes. int8 mean L2 norm down ~12% vs fp16. positive pair cosine mean 0.74 (fp16) -> 0.61 (int8). negatives similar -> margin reduced.

eva: can you try simple post-quant scale to recover norm?

anya: quick scalar *1.14 on embeddings lifts r@1 0.66->0.71 on holdout. risk of overfitting but promising.

carlos: small clusters pattern? length/token types?

anya: UMAP clusters are mostly queries <=4 tokens and many alphanumeric/code tokens. natural short queries less collapsed; code-ish queries collapse. KMeans k=200 purity drops 0.61->0.44 from fp16->int8.

ben: could be last-layer norm sensitivity or quantized activation clipping. check dequant path and when we normalize.

eva: also test keeping dequant in fp16 until after L2-normalize vs dequant->fp32->norm. implementation matters.

anya: current pipeline dequant->fp32->L2norm. ran fp16-dequant->norm path, +0.02 r@1. will run full sweep.

eval-bot: eval complete (r-2026-03-22-13): robinia-v1 int8 asymmetric r@1=0.70 r@5=0.87 silhouette=0.31 notes="asymmetric per-tensor helped but short-query tail still below threshold"

carlos: add UMAP png + per-length breakdown to onboarding doc. plan a canary: deploy fp16 staged, int8 behind fallback to albatross if r@1 < 0.7 on short queries.

eva: next steps: 1) per-channel vs per-tensor sweep with CalSet100k vs CalSet1M, 2) try 6-bit / QAT-style and per-channel bias correction, 3) learn small post-quant scaling on validation.

anya: I'll run the sweep, push results to the onboarding board, and include reproducible commands for SRE. if int8 can't meet short-query SLO we'll keep fp16 for Dedicated and use int8 for background batch embedding workloads.

ben: thanks. ping when sweep finishes and attach reproduce commands. :thumbsup:
